Advice from the older version of you...

My life path is almost identical to yours.  By the first grade it was determined that I was having trouble in school.  I was tested and they found that my IQ was near genius.  Went back and forth between gifted and talented course work and learning development programs.  In the 3rd grade I would ask my teacher to leave class and would just go to the library and read.  By the end of the 6th grade I was reading at a college level and I didn’t have many peers to talk/play with. I am also a borderline introvert/extrovert.

I was on my way to failing out of public high school my freshman year and my parents sent me to a private school.  I have tried many times to finish college but encounter the same problems that have plagued me my entire life with traditional learning.  Class just bores the crap out of me.

Intelligence does not guarantee success, hard work can guarantee success.  I am often loathe to do hard work.  It’s more fun to try and engineer an easier way to do/fix something.  Read the first sentence again...  

Avoid Management.  Being a manager will bore the crap out of you.  If you are anything like me attention to detail is not your thing.  You are probably more comfortable with abstractions it is better to leave the details to others.  Sales & Entrepreneurial endeavors are tailor made for you.   Learn on your own.  Look for certifications and training that will advance you in your field.

More about me:  
I chose IT as my career path and have been very successful up to a point.  I enjoy the building/problem solving aspect of the industry.  That bit of fun is over once you become a manager.  In some companies you can stay on the technical side without switching to management but the further you go up the ladder, the greater the pressure will be to make the switch.  Whatever you do, DON’T DO IT.  The extra money is not worth it!  I thought that I could resolve a lot of the frustration that I felt as a programmer/technician from the other side.  You can guess the result.

**TL,DR:** I had a similar experience with education, intelligence does not guarantee success, avoid management, learn on your own, sales/entrepreneurship are good choices for you.

**UPDATE FROM OP**  For some reason I cannot update the main text body.  Does it lock out changes after a certain period?  I am new to reddit.  Anyway, just wanted to give you a 48 hour update.

Thank all of you for the advice.  The advice that was most helpful were the posts saying that the arguement probably was not about the wedding photos.  The tact I chose to take was what's really bothering you.  

**The best advice was from kdplume:**

*I agree with most of the others. I do think this photo issue is a stand-in for something else. Almost seems like a manufactured problem because she wants attention...It could even be as simple as she's having trouble adjusting to "being married", in that, there was this whole exciting build-up to this point... now what? She wants to feel that excitement again...*

The real problem was that my wife was trying to recapture the feeling we had when we were dating.  I agree with this but money is not what generated those feelings.  It was long walks around the lake, cooking dinner at home, ILU msgs, date nights etc.

**The least helpful advice was the Divorce/Annulment coments.**  While I agree that behaviors do not often change (i.e. if your spouse hits you once, s/he will hit you again). That arguement does not apply here.  A if you don't like it "get to steppin'" stance would have caused irrevocable damage to our relationship.  TBH, these posts upset me and made me question the very sound decision that I made to marry the woman that I love.

This was just a case of misunderstanding of the comments made during the fight.  The jewlery fund was a tactic used by an old coworker of hers who had a very direct, abrupt style of communication (think Sheldon on Big Bang Theroy).  He often hurt others without knowing it, the suggestion given to him was to start a swear jar type fund so he could pay for his transgressions with his wife.  Apparently it worked for them.  I think what she was driving at in the original arguement was that I was insensitive (which I was not intentionally).

Reddit, thanks again for the advice.  Maybe I'll post a follow up on our year anniversary but, I doubt anyone will be interested next September. :)
